subject: TYPEDEF clause
notes: kb/Work PB1303 (wave 1012 J). cite.py --check 13.18.58.4 'The GLOBAL clause applies to the scope of the type-name' OK GR3; --check 8.4.6.2.2 'type-name described with a GLOBAL clause is a global name' OK. A GLOBAL type declaration is a global name: InheritStep.Seed, called by BinderDriver.BindUnitData BEFORE data.Bind, records every container's GLOBAL TYPEDEFs in the contained unit's InheritedGlobals slice (InheritedGlobals.AddContainerTypeDecls, nearest container first, a local declaration shadowing); DataBinder.TryFindTypeDecl is the ONE type-name lookup (TYPE clause, USAGE POINTER TO type-name, an intrinsic's type-name argument), the unit's own declarations first and the slice after (kb/Work PB2296). Golden: the directly contained and the grandchild program use OUTER's T (group with a numeric member and an 88) and the nearer MID's U over OUTER's U; the negative pins that a type-name WITHOUT GLOBAL stays local (COBOL1530). The object-definition clause of 8.4.6.2.2 (a type-name declared in a factory or instance definition is global to its methods) was probed and already conforms. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#InheritGlobalTypeDecls (kb/Work PB2296 moved the inherited GLOBAL type declarations into the InheritedGlobals slice; InheritGlobalTypeDecls is deleted and InheritedGlobals.AddContainerTypeDecls (called by InheritStep.Seed) is the same rule)
